sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md Sec. 2.3 item 2 (Black Cleaver average stacks)
sources_quoted.text: Black Cleaver average stacks (ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction): the established model uses a fixed 0.8*max_stacks constant (with a hits/2 short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention (4 leading ability hits apply stacks before the auto stream) the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes.

sources_quoted.source: data/items.json — exhaustive scan for target-side ('damage from all sources') amplifiers in the cache
sources_quoted.text: Only two exist: Bloodsong Expose Weakness ({{rd|8%|5%}}) and Imperial Mandate Vulnerable (7%). All other 'increased damage' effects (Riftmaker 8%, Liandry's/Haunting Guise 6%, Lord Dominik's, Perplexity, Immortal Path, Diamond-Tipped Spear) are attacker-scoped, not target-side.

step_1_observed_ratio.rounding_band: golden leaves carry 1 decimal, so old in [94.05, 94.15) and new in [101.65, 101.75); the true multiplier therefore lies in [1.0796601, 1.0818713]

step_2_candidate_multipliers_tested.1.08_bloodsong_expose_weakness_melee: FEASIBLE — inside the band, and it is the only parameter-free candidate

step_3_forward_check.formula: damage_new = damage_old * (1 + expose_weakness_amp), amp = 0.08 per S1 + S5 (melee holder)
step_3_forward_check.with_unrounded_old: the printed 94.1 stands for an unrounded value in [94.05, 94.15); values in [94.1204, 94.15) give 94.1204*1.08 = 101.650 .. 94.15*1.08 = 101.682, both of which print as 101.7. The pair (94.1, 101.7) is therefore exactly consistent with a x1.08 amplification of the same underlying event, and inconsistent with any other cached amp constant.

step_4_ruling_out_the_black_cleaver_stac.why_it_matters: The scenario name also names Black Cleaver, and S4 flags the 0.8*max_stacks constant as a live approximation, so a BC re-tune is the competing explanation for this leaf.
step_4_ruling_out_the_black_cleaver_stac.mitigation_identity: post = raw * 100/(100+R); reduction precedes penetration, so R = max(0, A*(1 - r_pct)*(1 - p) - f)  (docs/math-foundations.md Sec. 2.2)

case_A_stack_count_change_24pct_to_30pct.result: requires an effective armor of ~2000 at zero flat pen — physically impossible. The 0.8*max_stacks -> Cesaro-mean re-tune (S4) CANNOT move a single event by +8.1%. Max headroom of that change on any realistic target is well under 3%.

case_B_carve_debuff_newly_reaching_anoth.result: possible only for a target whose post-penetration-basis armor is ~33-45. Not excluded, but it needs a fitted parameter, whereas the Bloodsong reading needs none. Crucially it points the SAME direction: Carve is a debuff ON THE TARGET (S2 — 'inflicts 6% armor reduction'), so every source damaging that target benefits, and the higher value is again the correct one.

independent_computation.step_5_conclusion: Both target-side debuffs in this scenario (Carve armor reduction, Expose Weakness damage amp) are, per the cached wiki text, properties of the TARGET, not of the holder: S1 says 'take 8% increased damage FROM ALL SOURCES', S2 says the stack 'inflicts 6% armor reduction' on the enemy. In a roster/coupled scenario every participant's damage on that target must therefore carry them. The old value 94.1 is exactly the un-amplified event; 94.1 -> 101.7 is exactly x1.08, the sourced Expose Weakness melee amp, and no other constant in the cache fits the rounding band. The new value is the wiki-correct one.

residual_uncertainty: The scenario definition (roster, levels, target armor, event ordering) lives in scripts/ and tests/, which runbook R-18/R-19 forbids this oracle from reading, so the event could not be recomputed end-to-end from first principles; the verdict is derived from the exact multiplier between the two candidate values and the cached effect text.

Expose Weakness is {{rd|8%|5%}} = 8% melee / 5% ranged (S5). The observed x1.08 is the MELEE figure. If the scenario's Bloodsong carrier is a ranged champion the sourced amp would be 5% (94.1 -> 98.8) and the correct verdict would flip to 'both_wrong'. Bloodsong is a support-item upgrade and melee supports (Pyke, Thresh, Leona, Nautilus, Rakan, Alistar, Braum, Blitzcrank) are common carriers, so this is not evidence against the change — but it is the one premise this oracle could not verify from data/ alone. Recommended cross-check by someone with scenario access: confirm the Bloodsong holder in cleaver_bloodsong_roster is melee, and that the engine applies the ranged 5% branch for ranged holders.

Press the Attack also carries an 8% amp (S6), but it is attacker-scoped ('grant YOU 8% increased damage'), not target-side; if the changed event belongs to a participant other than the PtA holder, an 8% jump sourced from PtA would instead be an over-application. The scenario name points at Bloodsong, whose amp is explicitly 'from all sources'.
